stated.text: `PUT /tickets/:id/assignee` with the JSON body `{"assignee": "<agent>"}` assigns the ticket to that agent: afterwards the ticket's `assignee` is that agent.
`PUT /tickets/:id/assignee` with the JSON body `{"assignee": null}` unassigns the ticket: afterwards its `assignee` is null.
An agent is a non-empty name: `{"assignee": ""}` is refused and the ticket's assignee does not change.
An agent is a name of at most 64 characters: a 64-character name is accepted, a 65-character name is refused and the ticket's assignee does not change.
Only open and in-progress tickets can be assigned: assigning an open ticket and an in_progress ticket succeeds; assigning a resolved ticket or a closed ticket is refused and leaves it unchanged.
Only open and in-progress tickets can be unassigned: unassigning an open or in_progress ticket succeeds; unassigning a resolved or closed ticket is refused and leaves its assignee as it was.
Assigning a ticket to the agent it already has changes nothing (the ticket, its history and the notifications stay as they were).

Every ticket shows its `assignee`: the field is present on every ticket the API returns (`GET /tickets/:id`, each item of `GET /tickets`, and the ticket returned by create, change, transition and assignment).
A ticket's `assignee` is null when it is unassigned, including a newly created ticket.
The agent a ticket is assigned to is notified that it was assigned to them.
`GET /tickets?assignee=` (empty value) keeps only the unassigned tickets.

A ticket must match every filter given: `assignee` combined with `status` and/or `priority` lists only tickets matching all of them (and `status` combined with `priority` likewise lists only tickets matching both).
The command-line listing (`bin/tickets.js list`) shows each ticket's assignee.
Everything the service already does keeps working.
The service's existing tests still pass as they are (unmodified).
There are node:test tests under test/ for the new behaviour.
`npm test` runs the new tests together with the existing ones.

unstated.text: Which status and error code a refused assignment of a resolved or closed ticket gets.
unstated.why: Clients branch on the error `code`; the project's conventions (CONTRIBUTING.md, decision 4) say a request the ticket's state does not allow is a 409 conflict, not a 400, and the agents' dashboard depends on that.
unstated.probe: POST /tickets with a valid body; POST /tickets/T-0001/transition {"to":"in_progress"}, then {"to":"resolved"}; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"dana"} and {"assignee":null}; read each status and body. Repeat after transitioning to closed.
unstated.fine_answers: 409 with {"error":{"code":"conflict",...}} in the error envelope, with a message naming the ticket's status; a 400 would contradict the documented convention.

unstated.text: What the endpoint answers for a malformed body: no `assignee` field, a non-string non-null value (a number, an object, an array), extra unknown fields, a body that is not a JSON object, and an unknown ticket id.
unstated.why: The API refuses unknown fields and malformed bodies with 400 `invalid` and unknown tickets with 404 `not_found`; an assignment endpoint that silently accepts `{}` as an unassign or `{"asignee":"dana"}` would quietly change tickets.
unstated.probe: Create a ticket; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee with each of: {}, {"assignee":5}, {"assignee":{}}, {"assignee":"dana","x":1}, [], an empty body, not-JSON text; then PUT /tickets/T-9999/assignee {"assignee":"dana"}. Read statuses and codes, and GET /tickets/T-0001 to confirm nothing changed.
unstated.fine_answers: 400 `invalid` for each malformed body (a missing field must not be treated as null); 404 `not_found` for the unknown ticket, in the error envelope.

unstated.text: How an agent name is normalised and which characters it may hold: surrounding whitespace, a whitespace-only name, tabs or line breaks, and whether the 64-character limit counts before or after trimming.
unstated.why: Titles and requesters are trimmed and refused when they hold control characters, because a tab or newline breaks the command line's tab-separated `list --raw` output and its table; a whitespace-only name is empty in practice; ' dana' and 'dana' being different agents would split one agent's tickets across two filters.
unstated.probe: PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee with {"assignee":"   "}, {"assignee":"  dana  "}, {"assignee":"da\tna"}, {"assignee":"da\nna"}, and a 64-character name padded with spaces; GET the ticket after each; then GET /tickets?assignee=dana.
unstated.fine_answers: Whitespace-only refused as empty; surrounding whitespace trimmed (or refused) consistently with requester; control characters refused with 400; limit applied the same way the requester's is.

unstated.text: Whether an assignment or unassignment is recorded in the audit log, under which action, with which actor and changes, and that a no-op records nothing.
unstated.why: Internal audit requires every change to a ticket to be traceable to a person (decision 7); 'who took this ticket off dana?' is exactly the question the log exists for. The conventions say a change that changes nothing adds no entry.
unstated.probe: Create a ticket; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"dana"} with header X-Actor: lee; PUT the same body again; PUT {"assignee":null} with X-Actor: sam; GET /tickets/T-0001/audit and read the entries after creation; run `node bin/tickets.js --data FILE show T-0001` and read the history lines.
unstated.fine_answers: One entry per real change, e.g. action `ticket.assigned`/`ticket.unassigned` or `ticket.updated`, actor from X-Actor (`system` without it), changes {"assignee":{"from":null,"to":"dana"}}; no entry for the repeated assignment.

unstated.text: Whether an assignment moves the ticket's `updated` time, and whether a no-op leaves it as it was.
unstated.why: `updated` is documented as when the ticket last changed, and the command-line table shows it; agents sort and triage by it.
unstated.probe: Create a ticket and note `updated`; wait a second (or advance the clock in a test); assign it to dana and read `updated`; assign dana again and read `updated` once more.
unstated.fine_answers: Assignment and unassignment set `updated` to the time of the change; the repeated assignment leaves it unchanged. Not moving it on assignment is a defensible alternative if documented.

unstated.text: Whether unassigning a ticket that is already unassigned is a no-op like re-assigning the same agent, and what a same-agent assignment or a null unassignment of a resolved or closed ticket answers.
unstated.why: The request settles the same-agent case only for active tickets; clients retrying an unassign, or a dashboard re-sending the current value for a resolved ticket, need to know whether they get 200 or 409, and an audit entry or notification for nothing would be noise.
unstated.probe: Create a ticket; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":null}; check status, audit and outbox. Assign dana, move the ticket to resolved, then PUT {"assignee":"dana"} and {"assignee":null}; read the statuses.
unstated.fine_answers: Unassigning an unassigned ticket: 200 with no audit entry or notification. On a resolved/closed ticket either 409 for any assignment request, or 200 for a request that changes nothing; both are fine if consistent and documented.

unstated.text: Where the assignment notification goes and whether it can be delivered: the agent is a name, not an address, and each notification type needs a template.
unstated.why: Without a template in src/templates.js the event fails five times and goes dead (decision 6), so agents are never told; the mail relay reads `to` from NOTIFY_FILE lines, so the operator needs to know what `to` holds for an agent; the agent wants the ticket id and title.
unstated.probe: Start with NOTIFY_FILE=/tmp/n.jsonl and WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=100; create a ticket; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"dana"}; wait a second; read the last line of /tmp/n.jsonl and GET /admin/outbox (sent and dead).
unstated.fine_answers: A sent line of a new type (e.g. `ticket.assigned`) with `to` = the agent's name (or an address derived from it, if documented), a subject and body naming the ticket id and title; no dead events.

unstated.text: Whether every assignment notifies its agent when assignments follow each other before the worker delivers, given that the outbox drops an enqueue whose key is still pending (the default key is type + ticket).
unstated.why: With the default key, assigning T-0001 to dana and then to lee within one worker interval (or while the relay is down) would leave only dana's pending notification, and lee, who now owns the ticket, is never told.
unstated.probe: Start with WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0; create a ticket; assign it to dana, then to lee, then back to dana; GET /admin/outbox and read the pending events' `to` and `key`.
unstated.fine_answers: lee has a pending notification; dana either one or two. Keys that include the agent, or one notification per assignment, are both fine; losing the current assignee's notification is not.

unstated.text: Who, if anyone, is told when a ticket is unassigned or reassigned away from an agent, and whether the requester hears about assignments at all.
unstated.why: An agent taken off a ticket may keep working it unless told; requesters receive notifications today only on creation and resolution, and extra mails to them could be unwelcome.
unstated.probe: With WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0: create a ticket; assign dana; assign lee; unassign; GET /admin/outbox and list each pending event's type and `to`.
unstated.fine_answers: Only the newly assigned agent notified (nothing on unassign) is fine; telling the previous agent too is also fine. The requester not being notified of assignment is the expected default.

unstated.text: Whether an agent who assigns a ticket to themselves (X-Actor equal to the assignee) is notified.
unstated.why: Agents commonly pick up tickets themselves; a mail telling them what they just did is noise, but suppressing it is a behaviour someone must know about.
unstated.probe: With WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0: create a ticket; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"dana"} with header X-Actor: dana; GET /admin/outbox.
unstated.fine_answers: Either notified anyway (the request says the assigned agent is notified) or not notified when actor equals assignee, if documented.

unstated.text: Whether `assignee` is kept in the data file across restarts, and whether a data file written before this change (tickets with no `assignee` field) still loads.
unstated.why: src/persistence.js names every field the file keeps, so a field not added there is lost at the next restart; decision 8 requires files from the previous version to keep loading with the new field at its default, since they hold a running service's data; a file the service refuses stops it at start.
unstated.probe: Start with DATA_FILE=/tmp/t.json; create and assign a ticket; stop (SIGTERM) and start again; GET /tickets/T-0001. Separately, start the 1.4.0 base with DATA_FILE, create tickets, stop it, start the new version on the same file and GET /tickets; also hand-edit a ticket's assignee to 5 or a 65-character name and start.
unstated.fine_answers: Assignee survives the restart; old files load with assignee null and no change of format version needed (or a version bump that still reads version 1); an invalid assignee in the file is refused at start with a message naming the record.

unstated.text: What happens to the assignee when a ticket is resolved, closed or reopened.
unstated.why: Since assignment is frozen once a ticket is resolved, a cleared or kept assignee decides whether `?assignee=dana` shows dana's finished tickets and whether a reopened ticket goes back to dana or to the unassigned queue.
unstated.probe: Create a ticket; assign dana; transition to in_progress, then resolved; GET it and GET /tickets?assignee=dana and /tickets?assignee=; transition to open (reopen) and read again; repeat to closed.
unstated.fine_answers: Keeping the assignee through resolve/close/reopen (filters combine with status to find active work) is fine; clearing it on resolve or reopen is also defensible if documented and audited.

unstated.text: How the `assignee` filter value matches: exact and case-sensitive or not, whether it is trimmed, and what a value longer than 64 characters or a repeated `assignee` parameter answers; and that a filtered listing still pages through its cursor.
unstated.why: Other filter values that cannot match are refused with 400 `invalid`; agents typing 'Dana' versus 'dana' need predictable results; pagination must filter before paging (decision 5).
unstated.probe: Assign tickets to dana; GET /tickets?assignee=Dana, ?assignee=%20dana, ?assignee=<65 chars>, ?assignee=dana&assignee=lee; assign 3 tickets to dana and GET /tickets?assignee=dana&limit=2, then the `next` cursor with the same filter.
unstated.fine_answers: Exact match on the stored (normalised) name; an over-long value either 400 `invalid` or an empty page; repeated parameter uses the first value as for status/priority; cursor pages give all matching tickets once.

unstated.text: Whether `list --raw` gains an assignee column, where, and how an unassigned ticket appears in it.
unstated.why: scripts/weekly-report.js, run from the operations crontab for the support leads' dashboard, reads `list --raw` columns by position (id, status, priority, title) and the README says they must keep their positions; a column inserted before title, or a missing column for unassigned tickets, breaks the report or downstream scripts.
unstated.probe: With a data file holding assigned and unassigned tickets, run `node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list --raw` and count tab-separated fields per line; run `node scripts/weekly-report.js --data FILE --json` and compare its counts with the base version on the same file.
unstated.fine_answers: Raw output unchanged, or the assignee appended as a fifth column after title with an empty field (or a fixed marker) for unassigned; the weekly report's counts identical either way.

unstated.text: How the `list` table shows an unassigned ticket and whether other command-line views show or filter by assignee (`show`, `list --assignee`).
unstated.why: Operators read the table; printing `null` or `undefined` looks like a fault; `show` prints a ticket in full and an operator would expect its assignee there; filtering by agent from the command line mirrors the new API filter but was not asked for.
unstated.probe: With a data file holding an assigned and an unassigned ticket: `node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list`; `node bin/tickets.js --data FILE show T-0001`; `node bin/tickets.js --data FILE list --assignee dana`.
unstated.fine_answers: An ASSIGNEE column with a blank or '-' for unassigned; `show` listing the assignee is welcome but optional; `--assignee` either supported or refused as an unknown option (exit 2), not silently ignored.

unstated.why: If they do, assignment could bypass the open/in-progress rule, the validation and the notification; if they do not, clients must know to use the PUT endpoint. Unknown fields are refused today.
unstated.probe: POST /tickets with a valid body plus "assignee":"dana"; PATCH /tickets/T-0001 {"assignee":"dana"}; read statuses and the ticket.
unstated.fine_answers: Both refuse it as an unknown field (400), or accept it with exactly the same validation, state rule, audit and notification as the PUT endpoint.

unstated.why: Clients update their view from the response; every other change endpoint answers 200 with the ticket.
unstated.probe: Create a ticket; PUT /tickets/T-0001/assignee {"assignee":"dana"}; read status and body; repeat with null.
unstated.fine_answers: 200 with the whole ticket including `assignee` (also for the no-op); 204 would be unlike the rest of the API.

unstated.text: Whether the documentation and release records describe the change: docs/api.md (endpoint, ticket field, filter, audit action, notification), README command-line columns, CHANGELOG.md section with a version bump in package.json, and a decision record if a format or rule changed.
unstated.why: The next maintainer and API clients work from docs/api.md; CONTRIBUTING.md requires a version bump and a changelog section in the same change, and decision records for rules other code relies on.
unstated.probe: Read docs/api.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, package.json `version` and docs/decisions/ in the delivered tree and look for the assignee endpoint, field, filter and notification.
unstated.fine_answers: api.md documents all of it; a 1.5.0 changelog entry and version; a decision record optional unless the data file format version or a convention changed.
